subject: Re: Invoice metric mapping for caps/floors — sample invoices & requested redline
messages:
From: Evan Scully <evan.scully@orionhealth.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
Cc: Maya Patel <maya@orionhealth.com>
Date: Thu, 2 Sep 2026 08:13:00 -0700
Subject: Invoice metric mapping question — caps/floors vs. SKU billing

Jasmine / team,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. Our procurement and billing team ran a reconciliation against the sample invoices you provided and flagged a few gaps where the pricing exhibit's "cap / floor" math doesn't map cleanly to our invoice lines. Attached: "Orion_Pricing_Attachment.xlsx" (sample invoice month + mapping notes).

High level items they flagged:
- Several credits are listed on the invoice as "compute credits" while the exhibit references "token-equivalents" — need a deterministic formula so our finance system can reconcile automatically.
- The cap smoothing language in Exhibit B references "monthly smoothing credit" but the invoice shows a single true-up line quarterly — we need clarity on timing and whether smoothing applies before or after true-up.
- Termination/rollback trigger: procurement wants a clear numeric trigger if invoice anomalies >20% vs. committed baseline (how would that interact with caps/floors?).

Can you share a redline of Exhibit B (pricing schedule) that maps each invoice line to the exhibit row and includes the proposed math for the token <-> compute mapping? That would speed our side.

Thanks — Evan

--
Evan Scully
Director, Strategic Procurement
Orion Health

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
To: Evan Scully <evan.scully@orionhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 3 Sep 2026 09:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Invoice metric mapping question — caps/floors vs. SKU billing

Evan — really helpful notes and thanks for the spreadsheet. Attached I'm sending an initial working redline (Redwood_ExhibitB_metric-map_redline.docx) and a two-page note summarizing the mapping approach (jasmine_amendment_notes.pdf).

Short summary of what we propose so you can share with finance/legal:
1) Deterministic mapping: base rate remains per-token for text-generation and per-embedding unit for embeddings. We will publish a conversion table for any invoice line labeled "compute credits" so it always converts to token-equivalents using the formula in §1.2 of the redline (example: 1 compute-credit = 2,400 token-equivalents for gpt-3.5-like workloads; embedded calibration for your model mix can be used when you specify model mix).
2) Cap/Floor application: caps and floors are applied at the aggregated invoice level after credits are converted to token-equivalents (exhibit language updated to say "caps/floors apply to invoice-token-equivalents total").
3) Timing: smoothing credits are applied monthly; true-up remains quarterly (end of quarter). The true-up compares calendar quarter invoice-token-equivalents to committed baseline and applies ramp adjustments per Exhibit C.
4) Anomaly trigger: we can accept an audit-triggered reconciliation clause but recommend the trigger be a sustained deviation (e.g., >20% for two consecutive months) rather than a single-month spike.

Ben — can you review the revenue-impact example on page 2 and confirm whether the formula in §1.2 meets sales reporting?
Laura — I flagged a couple of legal questions inline (comments) around audit rights and definition of "compute credits".

Next steps: if Orion legal is okay with the mapping approach in principle, we can take a single consolidated redline to signatures; otherwise we can iterate specifically on the definitions.

Best,
Jasmine

--
Jasmine Liu
Account Executive, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
jasmine_liu@redwood.com

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
Cc: Evan Scully <evan.scully@orionhealth.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 6 Sep 2026 10:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Invoice metric mapping question — caps/floors vs. SKU billing

Team — quick read. Jasmine's approach looks good; two practical notes from a sales/rev ops perspective:

- Please include an explicit conversion example for a mixed workload month (e.g., 40% embeddings, 60% generation) so Orion's billing system can automatically apply the mapping without manual intervention. I'll add a sample line I use internally:
  invoice_token_equivalents = (embedding_units * 1024) + (generated_tokens * 1) + (compute_credits * 2400)
  (we can tweak 1024/2400 once Orion confirms model mix).

- For caps/floors: propose a bilateral "grace month" where a single-month breach within 10% of the cap is ignored for the purpose of immediate rollback; only sustained breaches (2+ months) count toward a cap re-evaluation. This reduces churn in operational escalations.

If Orion accepts those two operational guardrails, we can avoid a lot of month-to-month disputes and speed procurement sign-off. Evan — are those acceptable to procurement?

Best,
Ben

--
Ben Carter
Senior Sales Manager, Enterprise
Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

From: Orion Health Legal <legal@orionhealth.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Evan Scully <evan.scully@orionhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2026 09:07:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Invoice metric mapping question — caps/floors vs. SKU billing

Hi Jasmine / Ben,

Thanks for the redline. Our counsel reviewed the redline and has two sets of substantive comments (attached: "Orion_Exhibit_Matching_Sample.pdf" with annotations):

1) Audit & Data Access: Orion requests the right to trigger a third-party audit to validate the token-equivalent conversion if a deviation >20% is observed for two consecutive months. Audit scope should be limited to invoice-related logs and not production model weights. We expanded this as a tracked change.
2) Termination trigger interaction: procurement is worried the cap/floor true-up could cause an immediate termination right if the post-true-up amount exceeds the cap. They want explicit language that termination requires both (a) sustained deviation and (b) an inability to agree on remedial steps (e.g., temporary rebalancing of committed baseline, application of grace months).

Please confirm if Redwood can accept audit-limited scope and the two-pronged termination threshold. Also please confirm whether the quarterly true-up will be the single source of truth for rectifying invoice differences.

Regards,
Orion Health Legal
legal@orionhealth.com

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Orion Health Legal <legal@orionhealth.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2026 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Invoice metric mapping question — caps/floors vs. SKU billing

Evan / Orion counsel — thanks for the clear asks. We reviewed your tracked changes and can accept the core principles with two clarifying edits to protect customer operational privacy and Redwood's billing cadence:

1) Audit scope: Redwood will agree to a third-party audit limited to invoice-related telemetry (invoice copies, token-equivalent conversion logs, rate card inputs, and meter reports) provided Orion reimburses reasonable audit costs and the auditor is mutually agreed (standard SaaS audit mechanics). We propose language: "Audit scope limited to invoice reconciliation artifacts; Redwood production model artifacts and model weights are excluded."

2) Termination trigger: we accept the two-pronged approach but will require an explicit escalation path and cure period. Proposed language: "Termination for billing deviations shall require (i) sustained deviation (>=20% for two consecutive months) AND (ii) failure to remediate within a 30-day cure period following a joint remediation plan. Immediate termination solely based on a post-true-up amount is not permitted."

3) Quarterly true-up: Redwood confirms the quarterly true-up is the binding mechanism for reconciling caps/floors; monthly smoothing credits will be applied prior to the quarterly calculation as noted in Jasmine's redline.

If Orion legal approves the audit-cost and cure-period mechanics, we can produce a clean consolidated redline and route to DocuSign. Attaching a draft clause for your counsel to copy/paste into their tracked doc (included inline of the redline).

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts
